nodes.title: Security: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Security. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
flashcards.back: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, facilities, global infrastructure). Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud (data, IAM, OS patching on EC2, etc.).

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of AWS CloudTrail?
flashcards.back: CloudTrail records all API calls made to AWS services, providing an audit log of who did what, when, and from where. Essential for compliance and security investigations.

flashcards.front: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for, and which AWS service helps implement it?
flashcards.back: HTTPS uses TLS/SSL for encryption. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages free public SSL/TLS certificates for use with ELB, CloudFront, and API Gateway.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of AWS Shield?
flashcards.back: AWS Shield Standard: free, automatic DDoS protection for all AWS customers. Shield Advanced: paid, enhanced protection for EC2, ELB, CloudFront, Route 53 with the DDoS Response Team (DRT) and financial protection.

pairs.stem: What is the AWS Shared Responsibility Model's 'Security OF the cloud' vs 'IN the cloud'?
pairs.option: Of the cloud: AWS owns hardware, facilities, network. In the cloud: customer owns data, IAM, OS, app security

pairs.stem: What is the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
pairs.option: AWS secures the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, facilities); customers secure what they put into it

pairs.stem: What is the Principle of Least Privilege in AWS?
pairs.option: Grant administrator permissions broadly so engineers do not hit permission errors at runtime

pairs.stem: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for, and which AWS service helps implement it?
pairs.option: Speed — AWS Global Accelerator routes users over the AWS private global backbone

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of AWS CloudTrail?
pairs.option: Deploys and manages cloud infrastructure declaratively with YAML or JSON templates

pairs.stem: What is AWS CloudTrail?
pairs.option: A general-purpose log aggregation service that ingests application logs from any source

nodes.title: Compute: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Compute. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service allows you to run code without provisioning servers?
flashcards.back: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service. You upload code and Lambda runs it in response to events. You pay only for execution time — no server management required.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?
flashcards.back: Horizontal scaling (scale out/in) adds/removes instances. Vertical scaling (scale up/down) resizes the instance to a larger/smaller type. AWS Auto Scaling handles horizontal scaling.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Auto Scaling?
flashcards.back: AWS Auto Scaling monitors applications and automatically adjusts capacity (EC2 instances, ECS tasks, etc.) to maintain performance and minimize costs.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Elastic Load Balancing?
flashcards.back: ELB distributes traffic across multiple targets. ALB (Application) = Layer 7/HTTP, NLB (Network) = Layer 4/TCP, GLB (Gateway) = Layer 3 for third-party appliances. Integrates with Auto Scaling.

pairs.stem: What is AWS Elastic Load Balancing?
pairs.option: Distributes incoming traffic across EC2, container, IP, and Lambda targets for availability

pairs.stem: Which AWS service provides serverless container execution?
pairs.option: Amazon EKS managed Kubernetes control plane

pairs.stem: What is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?
pairs.option: An infrastructure-as-code tool that synthesizes templates from imperative code

pairs.stem: What is AWS Auto Scaling?
pairs.option: Automatically adjusts compute capacity by adding or removing instances based on demand

pairs.stem: Which AWS service allows you to run code without provisioning servers?
pairs.option: AWS Lambda

pairs.stem: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?
pairs.option: Horizontal scaling applies to relational databases; vertical applies to compute fleets

nodes.title: Storage: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Storage. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which AWS service provides scalable object storage?
flashcards.back: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is AWS's object storage service. It stores data as objects in buckets, offers 99.999999999% (11 9s) durability.

flashcards.front: What is Amazon EBS?
flashcards.back: EBS (Elastic Block Store) provides persistent block storage volumes attached to EC2. Unlike instance store, EBS persists after instance stop/terminate and can be detached/reattached.

flashcards.front: What is Amazon EFS?
flashcards.back: EFS (Elastic File System) is a managed NFS file system that can be mounted to multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones simultaneously. Unlike EBS which attaches to one instance.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Snowball?
flashcards.back: AWS Snowball is a secure, physical appliance for offline data migration. 80TB capacity. Snowball Edge adds compute. Snowmobile is a 100PB truck for exabyte migrations.

pairs.stem: What is Amazon EFS?
pairs.option: An elastic NFS file system that multiple EC2 instances can mount simultaneously

pairs.stem: What is AWS Snowball?
pairs.option: A CloudFront edge location that caches content close to end users

pairs.stem: What is Amazon FSx?
pairs.option: Managed file systems including FSx for Windows, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, and OpenZFS

pairs.stem: Which AWS service provides scalable object storage?
pairs.option: Amazon S3

pairs.stem: What is Amazon EBS?
pairs.option: Persistent block storage volumes for EC2 that outlive the instance and can be reattached

pairs.stem: What is AWS DataSync?
pairs.option: A managed database synchronization service that replicates RDS data across Regions

nodes.title: IAM: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on IAM. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to give an EC2 instance permission to read from one specific S?
flashcards.back: IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls authentication (who you are) and authorization (what you can do) in AWS through users, groups, roles, and policies.

flashcards.front: What is the principle of least privilege in AWS IAM?
flashcards.back: The principle of least privilege means granting only the permissions necessary to perform a task — nothing more. This minimizes the blast radius of compromised credentials.

flashcards.front: What is AWS IAM Role?
flashcards.back: IAM Roles are assumable identities with permissions. EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and cross-account users assume roles. No static credentials — uses temporary security tokens via STS.

flashcards.front: What is an IAM Policy Evaluation — what happens when Allow and Deny exist?
flashcards.back: AWS IAM policy evaluation: Any explicit Deny wins regardless of any Allow. This enables denying specific actions even for admins. All requests start as implicitly denied — Allows must be explicitly granted.

pairs.stem: What is the principle of least privilege in AWS IAM?
pairs.option: Grant users the minimum permissions required to perform their assigned tasks

pairs.stem: A developer needs to give an EC2 instance permission to read from one specific S3 bucket. Following AWS best practice, which approach should they use?
pairs.option: Identity and Access Management — who can do what in AWS

pairs.stem: What is an IAM Policy Evaluation — what happens when Allow and Deny exist?
pairs.option: Evaluation depends on the order in which IAM policies were attached to the principal

pairs.stem: What is the difference between AWS Managed Policies and Customer Managed Policies?
pairs.option: AWS Managed Policies and Customer Managed Policies behave identically at evaluation time

pairs.stem: What is AWS IAM Role?
pairs.option: An assumable IAM identity with permissions and short-lived credentials via STS

pairs.stem: What is IAM Access Analyzer?
pairs.option: A cost analysis tool that attributes spend to resources, accounts, tags, and services

nodes.title: Billing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Billing. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which tool helps estimate monthly AWS costs before deploying resources?
flashcards.back: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate monthly costs for AWS services before you deploy them. Cost Explorer analyzes existing costs; Budgets sets alerts.

flashcards.front: What is the AWS Free Tier?
flashcards.back: AWS Free Tier includes: 12-month free (new accounts) — e.g., 750hr/month EC2 t2.micro; Always free — e.g., 1M Lambda requests/month; Trial — e.g., 2 months Amazon Redshift.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Cost Explorer?
flashcards.back: Cost Explorer lets you analyze historical cost trends, identify cost drivers, forecast future spend, and find optimization opportunities with detailed filtering and charting.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Organizations?
flashcards.back: AWS Organizations enables centralized management of multiple AWS accounts: consolidated billing (volume discounts), Service Control Policies to restrict account permissions, and account grouping in OUs.

pairs.stem: What is the AWS Free Tier?
pairs.option: Limited free usage for 12 months on new accounts plus always-free and short trial offers

pairs.stem: What is the AWS Pricing Calculator?
pairs.option: A monthly cost savings report comparing actual spend to a defined budget baseline

pairs.stem: What is AWS Organizations?
pairs.option: A managed directory of IAM users with built-in single sign-on for the AWS Console

pairs.stem: What is AWS Cost Explorer?
pairs.option: A tool to visualize and analyze actual AWS cost and usage with granular filtering

pairs.stem: What is AWS Budgets?
pairs.option: A cost analysis tool that visualizes historical spend trends across services and tags

pairs.stem: Which tool helps estimate monthly AWS costs before deploying resources?
pairs.option: AWS Pricing Calculator

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of an Internet Gateway in a VPC?
flashcards.back: An Internet Gateway (IGW) is a horizontally-scaled, redundant VPC component that enables communication between VPC instances and the internet.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a Security Group and a Network ACL?
flashcards.back: SG: stateful (return traffic auto-allowed), instance level, allow rules only, evaluated as a whole. NACL: stateless (return traffic needs explicit rule), subnet level, ordered allow/deny rules. instance-level, allow-only rules. Network ACLs: stateless, subnet-level, allow AND deny rules

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of an AWS NAT Gateway?
flashcards.back: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet allows private subnet instances to reach the internet for updates/patches while remaining unreachable from inbound internet connections.

flashcards.front: What is VPC Peering vs Transit Gateway?
flashcards.back: VPC Peering: simple, low-cost, no transitive routing (A↔B and B↔C doesn't mean A↔C). Transit Gateway: scalable hub for 1000s of VPCs and VPNs with transitive routing, route tables, and multicast support.

pairs.stem: What is the purpose of an Internet Gateway in a VPC?
pairs.option: Provides outbound and inbound internet access for resources in public subnets

pairs.stem: What is Amazon CloudFront?
pairs.option: A global CDN with hundreds of edge locations caching content close to end users

pairs.stem: What is an EC2 Security Group?
pairs.option: A VPC route table entry that forwards specific destination CIDRs to a target gateway

pairs.stem: What is an AWS Availability Zone (AZ)?
pairs.option: A globally distributed CloudFront edge location that caches content close to end users

pairs.stem: What is an AMI (Amazon Machine Image)?
pairs.option: A template containing OS, applications, and configuration used to launch EC2 instances

pairs.stem: What is Amazon Route 53?
pairs.option: A scalable DNS and domain registration service with routing policies
